answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Audit**: each identity's action timing, peer set, and topic mix are hashed into a per-epoch fingerprint, and a new epoch only accepts identities whose fingerprint stays within a bounded canyon from their prior trajectory. A sudden jump or a flat, repetitive dune of near-identical behaviour flags the identity, which then must pass a costly re-earned beacon of fresh interaction history before acting again. Sybil farms pay repeated re-qualification rounds per fake identity, so scale becomes linearly expensive.
